summary: Code review PASS. RemoveAsync_ScopedDelete_DeletesOnlyMoviesInTargetFolder correctly exercises the two-phase cascade delete in production (collect deletedHashes from movies_filenames LIKE pattern, then DELETE movies WHERE hash IN deletedHashes). Hash A and B are correctly mapped to the target folder and deleted; Hash C has no movies_filenames entry so it survives. Test follows all established class conventions: [SkippableFact], Skip.If as first statement, OpenDirectConnection() for direct assertions, unique VI_TEST_SCOPEDEL_ hash constants. No blocking issues, no fix-forward changes required.

comments.note: Test setup inserts movies rows using ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE hash = @Hash (a no-op update) while the project's established pattern (DapperMovieCatalogRepository.InsertMovieAsync) uses INSERT IGNORE. Both are idempotent and functionally equivalent. Minor style inconsistency only; not worth bouncing.

The test correctly validates the two-phase cascade delete in production RemoveAsync: (1) collect hashes from movies_filenames matching the LIKE prefix, (2) delete movies rows for those hashes. Hash C has no movies_filenames entry so it is never added to deletedHashes and thus survives. The test scenario is well-chosen to cover both the positive deletion path and the non-deletion boundary.

No blocking or structural observations — test follows established class conventions (SkippableFact, Skip.If as first line, OpenDirectConnection(), unique hash constants with VI_TEST_ prefix, Dispose() cleanup). Three independent assertions with descriptive because: clauses.
